newsitem.title: USA: American States, others up on deal.
newsitem.headline: American States, others up on deal.

text.p: Shares of American States Financial Corp rose about 19 percent in very heavy trading after SAFECO Corp announced an agreement to buy the company for about $2.88 billion.
The price, at $47 a share, was well above analysts' expectations, triggering a rally in the shares of several other U.S. property-casualty insurers.
Shares of Ohio Casualty Corp rose 3-13/16, or nearly 10 percent, to 43-1/2. USF&G Corp rose 1-5/8, or more than seven percent, to 23-1/2.
"It raises the bar, it raises the valuation," Nutmeg Securities analyst Ira Zuckerman said.
However, Zuckerman said, other property-casualty insurers may not be able to command the high price that American States got.

SAFECO was willing to pay a higher price for American States because it expects to receive tax savings with a present value of $4-$5 a share for the writeoff of good will, bringing the actual price of the offer down to $42-$43 a share, SAFECO president Boh Dickey told Reuters earlier.
